transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

What brought me in is that I just can’t keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore, even when it really matters. At work, I’ll start trying to trace a client’s network problem, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve been rereading the same log entries over and over and I still don’t know what they say. It’s getting really frustrating.
Has this trouble focusing been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is it a new change compared to how your mind used to work?

It’s been there since I was a kid, honestly. My mother still jokes about my grade school report cards saying I was bright, but I wouldn’t stay in my seat, I’d blurt out answers, and I’d lose homework even when I’d actually done it. So… no, it doesn’t feel completely new.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling persistently low or sad, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure I’d say I’ve been persistently sad, no. Frustrated, definitely, but I haven’t really noticed a constant low mood or losing interest in things in that way.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things—more than most people would—and having trouble controlling that worry?
I don’t think so. I worry about things like anyone does, but it doesn’t feel like constant, uncontrollable worry about everything. That’s not really what’s been standing out to me.
Does this trouble focusing show up in other areas of your life too—like at home, in relationships, or during hobbies—or is it mainly limited to work?

It’s not just work, but work is where it’s most obvious. What really brought me in is that I can’t keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it, even when it matters. Like I’ll be tracing a client’s network problem, and ten minutes later I realize I’ve reread the same log entries three times and still don’t actually know what they say. It’s pretty frustrating.
These days, do you still notice things like fidgeting, feeling restless, or blurting out comments or interrupting others, similar to what you described as a child?

Yes, especially the interrupting part. I’ll cut people off even when I know I shouldn’t. In tech discussions, if the answer pops into my head, I start talking over them before they’re done explaining. Sometimes I’ll even reach for the keyboard or take over before they’ve finished showing me the problem. It’s not great, and I do notice it.
Have these attention and impulsivity issues caused any noticeable problems in your personal relationships or home life, such as friends or family commenting on it or conflicts arising because of it?

Yes. It’s caused problems, definitely. Since I lost the structure of my old job, people just don’t trust me to follow through like they used to. My reputation’s taken a pretty real hit.

I’ve lost freelance clients because I didn’t stay on top of things, and I missed out on a senior service-manager role. At home, my wife and I have had to worry about money more because of it. That’s been hard to face.
